---
title: "BED error-policy reader benchmark"
output: github_document
---

The public DuckBedQC `duckbedqc_118fc21` corpus supplies
`data/GRCh38_exons.bed` (SHA-256
`75b120e20be18497716c81d81648bb919574b34b90cc15abc474e06f09924073`,
22,802,546 bytes). Stage it with `scripts/stage_duckbedqc_data.sh`.
The baseline is an independent `origin/develop` worktree at
`r Sys.getenv("BED_POLICY_BASE_REV")` (`BED_POLICY_BASE`, its extension
build); the candidate source is `r Sys.getenv("BED_POLICY_REV")`
(`BED_POLICY_BRANCH`, its extension build). Both revisions are available in
this repository.
The query forces a full scan with `scan_mode := 'sequential'` and aggregates
`count(*)`, `sum(start)`, and `sum("end")`. Both numeric sums are checked across
policies and builds. Each run reads the 22 MB file and returns one aggregate
row. R/DBI wall time includes query planning and result materialization.
DuckDB R 1.5.5 loads the extension in a fresh R process for each build. The unindexed
file is clean under the reader's short-row rule. "default" is the engine's
unmodified thread setting, recorded alongside the single-thread runs.

The host mixes two core types, so the render records the CPU affinity of its
process, which every child R process inherits, in both observation files, and
compares with the previous render only on the same CPUs. Choose them with
`taskset -c`. `BED_POLICY_SIZE=reduced` runs a driver check: two scans per
cell and two alternating pairs, written to temporary files instead of
`bed_policy_observations.tsv` and `bed_policy_alternating.tsv`; it is not a
measurement.

``` sh
BED_POLICY_BASE=<baseline extension> BED_POLICY_BASE_REV=<baseline revision> \
BED_POLICY_BRANCH=<candidate extension> BED_POLICY_REV=<candidate revision> \
taskset -c 8-11 Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("benchmarks/benchmark_bed_policy.Rmd")'
```

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# The helper scripts and output paths are relative to the repository root.
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
```

```{r, echo=TRUE}
stopifnot(nzchar(Sys.getenv("BED_POLICY_BASE")),
          nzchar(Sys.getenv("BED_POLICY_BRANCH")),
          nzchar(Sys.getenv("BED_POLICY_REV")),
          nzchar(Sys.getenv("BED_POLICY_BASE_REV")))
size <- Sys.getenv("BED_POLICY_SIZE", "full")
if (!size %in% c("full", "reduced")) stop("BED_POLICY_SIZE must be full or reduced")
full_size <- identical(size, "full")
scans_per_cell <- if (full_size) 11L else 2L
alternating_pairs <- if (full_size) 15L else 2L
observations_path <- if (full_size) "benchmarks/bed_policy_observations.tsv" else tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
alternating_path <- if (full_size) "benchmarks/bed_policy_alternating.tsv" else tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
# The CPUs this process may run on, as taskset prints them; child processes
# inherit the mask.
affinity_line <- system2("taskset", c("-pc", Sys.getpid()), stdout = TRUE)
affinity <- sub("^.*: *", "", affinity_line[[length(affinity_line)]])
run_benchmark <- function(extension, label, revision) {
  output <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
  result <- system2("Rscript", c("benchmarks/bed_policy_run.R", extension,
                                   label, revision, output, scans_per_cell))
  if (!is.null(attr(result, "status")) && attr(result, "status") != 0L) {
    stop("benchmark failed: ", label)
  }
  read.delim(output, check.names = FALSE)
}
observations <- rbind(
  run_benchmark(Sys.getenv("BED_POLICY_BRANCH"), "candidate",
                Sys.getenv("BED_POLICY_REV")),
  run_benchmark(Sys.getenv("BED_POLICY_BASE"), "baseline",
                Sys.getenv("BED_POLICY_BASE_REV"))
)
stopifnot(length(unique(observations$input_lines)) == 1L,
          length(unique(observations$output_rows)) == 1L,
          length(unique(observations$start_sum)) == 1L,
          length(unique(observations$end_sum)) == 1L,
          all(table(interaction(observations$build, observations$threads,
                                observations$policy, drop = TRUE)) == scans_per_cell))
observations$affinity <- affinity
write.table(observations, observations_path,
            sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
summary <- aggregate(seconds ~ revision + build + threads + effective_threads +
                       policy + input_lines + output_rows,
                     observations, median)
summary$seconds <- round(summary$seconds, 4)
knitr::kable(summary, caption = sprintf("Median wall seconds over %d independent scans per policy/thread/build",
                                        scans_per_cell))
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
for (thread_setting in c("1", "default")) {
  baseline <- subset(summary, build == "baseline" & threads == thread_setting &
                       policy == "error")$seconds
  candidate <- subset(summary, build == "candidate" & threads == thread_setting &
                        policy == "error")$seconds
  cat(sprintf("Default policy, %s threads: %.3f s to %.3f s (%+.1f%%).\n\n",
              thread_setting, baseline, candidate, 100 * (candidate / baseline - 1)))
}
```

The alternating comparison runs the exact default-policy aggregate with
one DuckDB thread in a fresh R process per observation. The baseline and
candidate alternate fifteen times each (twice in a reduced run); process
startup is outside the reported query wall time.

```{r alternating}
load_at_start <- system("uptime", intern = TRUE)
run_single <- function(extension, label, run) {
  lines <- system2("Rscript", c("benchmarks/bed_policy_single.R",
                                  extension, label, run), stdout = TRUE)
  if (!is.null(attr(lines, "status")) && attr(lines, "status") != 0L) {
    stop("alternating scan failed: ", label, " run ", run)
  }
  read.delim(text = paste(lines, collapse = "\n"), check.names = FALSE)
}
alternating <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(alternating_pairs), function(run) {
  rbind(run_single(Sys.getenv("BED_POLICY_BASE"), "baseline", run),
        run_single(Sys.getenv("BED_POLICY_BRANCH"), "candidate", run))
}))
stopifnot(nrow(alternating) == 2L * alternating_pairs,
          length(unique(alternating$result)) == 1L,
          all(table(alternating$build) == alternating_pairs))
alternating$affinity <- affinity
write.table(alternating, alternating_path,
            sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
alternating_summary <- aggregate(seconds ~ build, alternating,
                                 function(x) c(min = min(x), median = median(x)))
alternating_summary <- data.frame(
  build = alternating_summary$build,
  min = round(alternating_summary$seconds[, "min"], 4),
  median = round(alternating_summary$seconds[, "median"], 4)
)
knitr::kable(alternating_summary,
             caption = sprintf("Alternating fresh-process scans (%d per build, one thread)", alternating_pairs))
```

Host load before alternating scans: `r load_at_start`. CPU affinity: `r affinity`.
`r if (!full_size) "**Reduced driver check (BED_POLICY_SIZE=reduced): not a measurement.**"`

The reader's only fatal data-line check is fewer than three tab-delimited
fields. Numeric parse failures yield NULL and reversed intervals are not
rejected. This workload does not measure malformed-row reporting or remote I/O.

## Change from the previous render

```{r previous, echo=FALSE}
# The previous render of this report, read from git. Its candidate was the
# BED error-policy branch; since then read_bed, the fasta_nuc BED input,
# mosdepth --by and duckhts_bam_bed_coverage parse BED lines through one shared
# helper. The host mixes core types, so the comparison needs the same CPUs.
previous_revision <- "8ca12e37"
read_previous <- function(file) {
  text <- system2("git", c("show", paste0(previous_revision, ":benchmarks/", file)), stdout = TRUE)
  stopifnot(is.null(attr(text, "status")))
  utils::read.delim(text = paste(text, collapse = "\n"), check.names = FALSE,
                    colClasses = "character")
}
previous_observations <- read_previous("bed_policy_observations.tsv")
previous_alternating <- read_previous("bed_policy_alternating.tsv")
previous_affinity <- unique(c(previous_observations$affinity, previous_alternating$affinity))
if (length(previous_affinity) && !identical(previous_affinity, affinity)) {
  stop("The previous render ran on CPUs ", paste(previous_affinity, collapse = ", "),
       " and this one on CPUs ", affinity, "; render with taskset -c ", previous_affinity[[1L]])
}
# The default thread count follows the host; compare by setting and show it.
cell_medians <- function(x) {
  x$seconds <- as.numeric(x$seconds)
  aggregate(seconds ~ build + threads + effective_threads + policy, x, median)
}
previous_scans <- merge(cell_medians(previous_observations), cell_medians(observations),
                        by = c("build", "threads", "policy"), suffixes = c("_before", "_after"))
stopifnot(nrow(previous_scans) > 0)
previous_scans$time_ratio <- previous_scans$seconds_after / previous_scans$seconds_before
previous_scans <- previous_scans[order(previous_scans$build, previous_scans$threads, previous_scans$policy), ]
rownames(previous_scans) <- NULL
previous_pairs <- merge(aggregate(seconds ~ build, transform(previous_alternating, seconds = as.numeric(seconds)), median),
                        aggregate(seconds ~ build, alternating, median),
                        by = "build", suffixes = c("_before", "_after"))
stopifnot(nrow(previous_pairs) == 2L)
previous_pairs$time_ratio <- previous_pairs$seconds_after / previous_pairs$seconds_before
cpu_note <- if (!length(previous_affinity)) {
  "The previous render recorded no CPU affinity, so the CPUs it ran on are unknown and the ratios may include a change of core type."
} else {
  paste0("Both renders ran on CPUs ", affinity, ".")
}
```

The previous render, `r previous_revision`, ran the same scans of the same
file with the same driver and host, with candidate
`r unique(previous_observations$revision[previous_observations$build == "candidate"])` and baseline
`r unique(previous_observations$revision[previous_observations$build == "baseline"])`;
"candidate" and "baseline" name different revisions in the two renders.
`r cpu_note` Host load differs between renders. Median wall seconds per cell:

```{r previous_scans, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(previous_scans, digits = 4)
```

Alternating fresh-process scans, median per build:

```{r previous_pairs, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(previous_pairs, digits = 4)
```
